h1.say: If you've prayed for fifteen years, you've recited Al-Fatiha more than ninety thousand times.

h2.say: Seventeen times a day, every single day. But if someone stopped you and asked what one of its words means, could you tell them?

h3.say: By the end of this video, you'll know every word. All twenty-nine of them.

h4.say: And here's why it's worth it. The words in these seven verses appear almost ten thousand times across the Quran. That's one in every eight words you'll ever read in it.

h5.say: So let's go through it, one ayah at a time.

1:1:1.say: Bismi. In the name. The bi at the front means in, or with. And ism means name.

1:1:2.say: Allah. The most frequent name in the entire Quran. Two thousand, six hundred ninety-nine times.

1:1:3.say: Ar-Rahman. The Entirely Merciful. It comes from the root ra, ha, meem, the root of mercy.

1:1:4.say: Ar-Raheem. The Especially Merciful. Same root, different form. Ar-Rahman is used only for Allah, while raheem can describe a person too.

a1-tr.say: In the name of Allāh, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

1:2:1.say: Al-hamdu. The praise. Al simply means the, and you'll see it on almost every line of the Quran.

1:2:2.say: Lillahi. Li means to, or for. So this is: to Allah.

1:2:3.say: Rabbi. Lord. But rabb holds much more than one English word: owner, master, sustainer, provider, caretaker. It appears nine hundred seventy-five times.

1:2:4.say: Al-'alameen. The worlds. Its root, ayn, lam, meem, is the same root as 'ilm, knowledge.

a2-tr.say: [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, Lord of the worlds.

a3-known.say: Ar-Rahman, ar-Raheem. You already know both of these words. That's the power of learning the Quran's vocabulary: it keeps coming back.

a3-tr.say: The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful,

1:4:1.say: Maaliki. Master, or Sovereign. Its root, meem, lam, kaf, also gives us malik, king, and mulk, dominion.

1:4:2.say: Yawmi. Day. Yawm appears four hundred seventy-five times, so it is one of the most useful words you can learn.

1:4:3.say: Ad-deen. Recompense. Yawm ad-deen is the Day when everything we earned, good or bad, is repaid.

a4-tr.say: Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.

1:5:1.say: Iyyaka. You. And notice that it comes first. Arabic could have said, we worship You. Putting You first gives the meaning: You alone.

1:5:2.say: Na'budu. We worship. The na at the start means we. And its root, ayn, ba, dal, also gives us 'abd, a servant.

1:5:3.say: Wa-iyyaka. Wa means and. And You alone.

1:5:4.say: Nasta'een. We ask for help. There's that na again: we.

a5-tr.say: It is You we worship and You we ask for help.

1:6:1.say: Ihdina. Guide us. This time the na is on the end, and it means us. Words from the root of guidance appear over three hundred times.

1:6:3.say: Al-mustaqeem. The straight. It comes from the root of qama, to stand upright.

a6-tr.say: Guide us to the straight path.

1:7:1.say: Sirata. Path. The same word again, so you already know it.

1:7:2.say: Alladheena. Those who. This word appears almost fifteen hundred times.

1:7:3.say: An'amta. You have bestowed favor. The ta on the end means you.

1:7:4.say: 'Alayhim. Upon them. 'Ala means on, and him means them.

1:7:6.say: Al-maghdoobi. Those who have earned anger.

1:7:8.say: Wa-la. And not. La on its own appears over seventeen hundred times.

1:7:9.say: Ad-dalleen. Those who are astray. And that's the whole surah.

a7-tr.say: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have earned [Your] anger or of those who are astray.

r1.say: That's all twenty-nine words. Now listen to the whole surah one more time, and follow the meaning as you hear it.

o1.say: Next time you pray, you won't just hear these words. You'll understand them.

o2.say: You just learned twenty-three different words, and together they make up one in eight words of the Quran. The five hundred most common words cover eighty percent of it.

o3.say: That's what Quranki is for. It teaches the Quran's words in the order the Quran uses them, with spaced repetition so they stick. It's free at quranki dot org, on iPhone, and on Android.

o4.say: If this helped, subscribe, and we’ll go through the next surah, word by word.
